name: Knowing when models are uncertain
gist: Papers studying how to measure and communicate what a model doesn't know—calibration, uncertainty bounds, and confidence scores that readers can trust.
explain: A model that always outputs a guess, even when it has no confidence, is dangerous. If a medical AI diagnoses disease with the same certainty for a clear X-ray and a blurry one, doctors can't know which diagnosis to trust. If a self-driving car is equally sure about the distance to an obstacle whether the camera is clear or obscured by rain, it will crash. The solution is uncertainty quantification — making the model express how confident it is, not just what it thinks the answer is.

The challenge is that confidence is not obvious from a model's output. A neural network might output the same probability for a prediction whether it has seen similar examples a thousand times or never at all. Real uncertainty has many layers: uncertainty about what the input actually is (the rain on the camera), uncertainty about whether the model has learned the right pattern (did it learn the real rule or memorize examples), and uncertainty about the world itself (the thing you are trying to predict is inherently noisy or random). You need techniques to capture all of these kinds of uncertainty, not just report a single confidence number that could be meaningless.

Researchers build uncertainty estimates using multiple approaches. Some train many models and look at how much their predictions disagree — if they all agree, probably they are right, if they all disagree, probably the input is ambiguous. Some use probability theory to model not just what the prediction should be but how much uncertainty there is around it. Some measure calibration — whether a model that says it is 90% confident really is correct 90% of the time. The goal is a confidence score that a human can actually act on.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Long-Tailed Classification
papers.contribution: Guarantees marginal coverage while achieving reasonable set sizes on long-tailed datasets like Pl@ntNet-300K and iNaturalist-2018 with 1,081 and 8,142 classes respectively.

papers.title: End-to-End Probabilistic Framework for Learning with Hard Constraints
papers.contribution: Applies to PDE learning with uncertainty estimates and probabilistic time-series forecasting while handling non-linear constraints without distributional assumptions.

papers.title: Nonparametric Distribution Regression Re-calibration

papers.title: Post-hoc Probabilistic Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Provides improved and well-calibrated predictive uncertainties, interpretable uncertainty estimates, and sample-efficient active learning for safety-critical applications.

papers.title: Bayesian Evidence-Driven Prototype Evolution for Federated Domain Adaptation
papers.contribution: Achieves superior performance on multiple cross-domain datasets with strong expressiveness and generalization capability in heterogeneous domains.

papers.title: Efficient Autoregressive Inference for Transformer Probabilistic Models

papers.title: Efficient Credal Prediction through Decalibration
papers.contribution: Decalibration enables credal prediction on TabPFN and CLIP architectures (previously infeasible), with strong coverage-efficiency performance, OOD detection, and in-context learning capabilities.

papers.title: Robustness of Probabilistic Models to Low-Quality Data: A Multi-Perspective Analysis
papers.contribution: Shows autoregressive models are remarkably resilient while diffusion models degrade catastrophically, linked to conditioning information richness and absolute information content.

papers.title: Spatial Conformal Inference through Localized Quantile Regression
papers.contribution: Achieves near-nominal coverage with tighter and more stable prediction intervals than existing methods on synthetic and real spatial datasets.

papers.title: TabMGP: Martingale Posterior with TabPFN
papers.contribution: Produces credible sets with near-nominal coverage and outperforms both handcrafted MGP constructions and standard Bayesian baselines.

papers.title: Tokenised Flow Matching for Hierarchical Simulation Based Inference
papers.contribution: Well-calibrated posteriors on hierarchical SBI benchmark and realistic infectious disease/CFD models while reducing computational cost through likelihood factorization.

papers.title: Uncertainty Estimation via Hyperspherical Confidence Mapping
papers.contribution: HCM provides deterministic and interpretable uncertainty estimates applicable to regression and classification, with competitive performance to ensemble and evidential approaches while reducing inference cost.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Diagnostics for Physics-Informed Machine Learning
